title: Predictive Cost & Latency Surface Matrix — Operator Guidance
author: Aisha Kaur
body:
Summary:
This document defines the predictive cost/latency surface matrix for platform LLM inference traffic and provides a concrete operator guidance playbook for calibrating dashboards, tuning alert thresholds, and running controlled experiments that impact prefetch/caching, eviction and model-variant routing. The goal is to make threshold decisions explainable, reversible, and aligned to tenant SLAs and cost budgets.

Audience:
- Platform operators
- Observability engineers
- Oncall and SRE
- Product managers owning tenant SLAs and pricing signals

Scope:
Covers: per-tenant and cluster-level cost vs. latency tradeoffs for common request categories (foreground low-context, foreground long-context, batch embeddings), required dashboard panels, recommended alerting rules and escalation workflow, calibration procedure and a short experiment template. Does NOT replace individual service runbooks for model-swap emergencies — see related runbooks.

Definitions and key signals:
- surface point: (q, s, m) tuple where q=request category, s=sequence-length bucket, m=model-variant.
- Q categories: foreground-latency (interactive), foreground-throughput (long sequence), batch-embedding (async), rerank (short cached).
- Core signals: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens-per-request (avg), tokens-per-second (cluster), avg-gpu-util, prefix-kv-hit-rate, token-cost-per-request (USD), request-success-rate (200s / total).

Recommended SLOs (examples — translate per-customer):
| Category | p50 | p95 | p99 | success-rate SLO | cost-sensitivity |
|----------|-----|-----|-----|------------------|------------------|
| foreground-latency | 40ms | 120ms | 250ms | 99.9% | high |
| foreground-long | 120ms | 400ms | 1,200ms | 99.5% | medium |
| batch-embedding | n/a | n/a | n/a (throughput SLO) | 99.0% | very-high |

Surface matrix template (operator view):
For each (q, s, m) surface point capture these baseline columns as dashboard filters:
- baseline p50/p95/p99 (rolling 30d)
- burst multiplier (current window / baseline 5m)
- prefetch KV hit-rate (0–100%)
- avg tokens/request and tokens/sec
- estimated token USD cost (model + infra) per request
- failure mode tag (OOM, eviction, timeouts)

Dashboards (panel library):
Create an "Inference Surface" Grafana board composed of:
1) Surface heatmap: rows=model-variants, cols=sequence-length buckets; color = p99 latency normalized by SLO (value >1 = violation).
2) Cost-sensitivity strip: per-tenant cost delta if moving to next-cheaper variant (estimate formula displayed).
3) Prefetch KV hit-rate trend + operator-annotated maintenance windows.
4) Eviction events timeline (annotated by model version rollouts).
5) Composite alert scoreboard (active alerts, SLO burn rate per tenant).
6) Synthetic lab panel: run controlled synthetic workloads and show baseline vs experiment.

Example PromQL alert recipes (tune thresholds to environment):
- Alert: surface-p99-violation-high
  Expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{le, model_variant, job="inference"}[5m])) by (le, model_variant)) > 1.0
  For: 5m
  Labels: severity=page, owner=platform-operators
  Annotation: "p99 exceeding configured SLO for model_variant={{ $labels.model_variant }}; check prefetch hit-rate and eviction logs."

- Alert: kv-hit-rate-drop
  Expr: avg_over_time(kv_hit_rate{service="prefetch"}[10m]) < 0.6
  For: 10m
  Labels: severity=sev2
  Annotation: "Probable cache degradation; review prefetcher and Redis/metadata latency."

Alert tuning guidance:
- Use burn-rate derived SLOs for noisy signals (p95/p99): e.g., configure SLO burn alerts when 14-day burn-rate > 1.0 and 30-min burn-rate > 3.0.
- Add a recovery condition: cancel page if p99 returns under 80% of SLO for 15m.
- Correlate p99 alerts with token-cost deltas: If p99 violation coincides with >20% cost increase, consider temporary model-rollforward to a cheaper stable variant with documented quality delta.

Operator runbook: threshold calibration workshop (90 minutes)
1) Prep (15m): pick 3 representative tenants (one small, one mid, one large) and load 30d baseline metrics into the synthetic lab panel.
2) Discovery (20m): for each tenant, map top 10 request prefixes by token consumption and annotate current model_variant mapping.
3) Hypothesis (15m): propose one change per tenant (e.g., lower prefetched KV retention from 10s to 2s; try quantized model_variant for batch embeddings). Write down expected cost delta and latency risk.
4) Controlled test (25m): execute experiment against 1% of traffic or in synthetic lab. Observe 30m rolling metrics.
5) Decision & roll plan (15m): if cost drops >=10% and p99 increases <10% and success-rate unaffected, schedule gradual rollout with canary and automatic rollback conditions.

Operator runbook: emergency mitigation (short form)
1) If p99 > 2x SLO and request-success-rate < 95% for >10m:
  a) Check prefetcher KV hit-rate and recent eviction spikes.
  b) If eviction spike present: throttle batch and long-foreground queues by 30% using runtime quota escape hatch.
  c) If KV hit-rate low: temporarily expand prefix cache TTLs or fallback to model-variant pinned in cold cache.
  d) If model OOM observed: immediately switch traffic to next-compatible model-variant with known quality delta; create incident and page ML-developer oncall.
2) Post-stabilize: collect traces, annotate incident timeline, and file a short retro entry in the retrospective board (tag: incident-llm-surface).

Experimentation recipes (examples):
- Quantization A/B for embeddings: route 10% of embedding load to q8_variant, measure retrieval AUC on a fixed eval set, cost delta, and latency p95.
- Prefetch TTL sweep: run five TTL values [0.5s, 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s] on synthetic replay and compute cost/latency per TTL.
- Model-compression fallback: test a smaller model_variant for high-length tails and compute quality delta vs user-facing metrics.

Quality and rollback criteria (must be explicit in every experiment):
- Quality gate: downstream eval metric (rerank accuracy or embedding cosine recall) cannot degrade by >2% absolute for broadly impacting customers unless pre-approved.
- Latency gate: p99 must not increase by more than 15% for foreground-latency category.
- Cost gate: expected cost reduction must be >=8% to justify potential small quality hits.
- Automatic rollback: any sustained success-rate drop >1% for 10m triggers immediate rollback.

Operational telemetry checklist (must be onboarded to the board):
- request_duration_p50/p95/p99 by model_variant and tenant
- kv_hit_rate, kv_miss_latency_ms by cache-shard
- eviction_count and eviction_reason by node and tenant
- model_gpu_mem_pressure_pct and OOM events
- token_cost_estimate_per_request (running estimate)
- synthetic load experiment results and annotated diff from baseline

Maintenance and accountability:
- Quarterly calibration: SRE + Observability + Applied ML run the calibration workshop; notes stored under team-wiki/calibration-workshops.
- Ownership: Observability owns dashboards; Platform SRE owns alert rules; Applied ML owns model-variant quality gates.
- Audit: every threshold change must include: author, justification, experiment id, and rollback plan.

Roadmap items (next 12 months):
- H1 2026: Add model-quality metadata to surface matrix (per-variant eval curves) and auto-suggest cheaper variants with estimated quality delta.
- H2 2026: Rollout per-tenant simulated cost impact preview in the dashboard (what-if for 30d baseline).
- H2 2026: Integrate runbook automation: one-click canary creation and auto-rollback via orchestration service.

Appendix: sample PromQL snippets and synthetic load command
- Sample token-cost estimate (pseudo):
  token_cost_per_request = model_token_price * avg_tokens + gpu_infra_cost_per_token_estimate

- Synthetic load example (CLI):
  echo '{"prompt":"<sample>", "n":1}' | loadgen --target=https://inference-internal.svc.local --rps=20 --concurrency=50 --model=mistral-small --duration=300s

- PromQL for eviction spikes:
  increase(eviction_count{job="inference"}[5m]) > 0

Document maintenance:
- This doc is reviewed quarterly; next scheduled review 2026-05-01.
- Keep experiment artifacts under /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/calibration-workshops/ with experiment IDs referenced from here.
